title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated repair step increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation versus accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) under a shared_initial estimand using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator. Each pair used one shared LLM candidate evaluated under (a) baseline — accept single shot, and (b) guarded — run deterministic validation and allow at most one constrained automated repair. Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Deterministic rescue occurred once (a sequencing omission corrected by a single constrained edit). Under this synthetic suite and a ≤1‑repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We release the preregistration, execution, validator traces, and analysis artifacts with the archived run bundle.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly applied to NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, templated synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness (sequencing constraints, reachability, and policy preservation) matters operationally and exceeds what simple syntactic checks capture. A common engineering pattern pairs generative models with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce deployment risk. However, the measurable benefit of such guarded pipelines depends on (i) estimand conditioning (what is held fixed), (ii) single‑shot generator quality, (iii) validator expressiveness, and (iv) the permitted repair budget. We preregistered a paired experiment (cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) isolating the deterministic rescue attainable when the identical single LLM draw per intent is evaluated under two treatments: baseline (accept single shot) and guarded (deterministic validator + ≤1 automated repair). Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired evaluation under a shared_initial estimand that conditions on one LLM draw per intent; (2) a complete execution and analysis bundle including deterministic validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; and (3) an evidence‑grounded discussion of estimand conditioning, ceiling effects, and operational implications for NetOps pre‑deployment pipelines.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers document rapid progress in LLM applications for network management, intent translation, and automated configuration synthesis, and they emphasize tool augmentation (planner‑centric, ReAct‑style) to coordinate external validators and simulators [1]–[3]. Empirical reports demonstrate that generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness relative to unconstrained generation, but reported gains depend on validator coverage, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [4], [5]. Work on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets highlights detection approaches (semantic‑entropy detectors, retrieval augmentation, self‑reflection) that reduce false positives in high‑stakes domains but whose transfer to complex NetOps settings depends on validator semantics and threat models [6]. Hybrid repair approaches that combine symbolic fault localization or formal checks with generative repair operators show promise but yield variable success across fault classes and benchmarks [2], [4]. Our study isolates the bounded deterministic rescue from a verifier+constrained‑repair operator under a shared_initial estimand — complementing prior work that conflates validation benefits with resampling or interactive regeneration [2], [3].
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered the confirmatory paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) and froze the primary estimand: absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents after applying prespecified inclusion/exclusion rules. The preregistration (archived) fixed the analysis executor, multiplicity plan, and failure/exclusion handling. Task generation and stratification. A deterministic task generator produced a synthetic topology suite stratified into three difficulty strata (low/medium/high) with 100 paired intents per stratum. Each manifest encodes the natural‑language intent, initial and expected final device states, sequencing invariants (required_sequence), protected interfaces, and difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). Shared_initial generation protocol. To isolate deterministic rescue from resampling effects we implemented a shared_initial estimand: for each pair the adapter produced exactly one shared_initial candidate (one LLM draw) that was reused verbatim for both baseline and guarded conditions. Generator and configuration. The requested generation model was gpt-5-mini; the run configuration limited reasoning effort and set a bounded output token budget. Deterministic validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic validator implementing a full_intent_constraint_validation rule that checks sequencing invariants, required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability invariants, and protected‑interface constraints. The guarded pipeline allowed at most one automated repair attempt (repair budget ≤ 1). The repair operator was a constrained edit routine limited to localized sequencing and insertion edits and applied only when the validator flagged the shared_initial candidate. Scoring and contingency. The primary outcome is binary: an unflagged candidate is a pass. For each pair we record whether baseline and guarded conditions are unflagged and assemble the paired contingency table (n11, n10, n01, n00). Analysis and inferential procedures. The preregistered confirmatory executor computed contingency counts, the absolute paired difference, an exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant pairs, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000). Sensitivity analyses (planned) include failure‑as‑zero handling for single‑call failures and exploratory stratum‑wise tests with multiplicity control. Execution controls. The execution adapter enforced the shared_initial protocol, the single‑repair budget, deterministic contamination checks (negative controls), and the preregistered inclusion/exclusion rules (pairs excluded only if both pipeline calls failed due to provider/outage). Instrumentation logged stage counts and model‑call accounting for later audit.
sections.results: Execution accounting. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with planned_episode_count = 600 and completed_episode_count = 600, yielding complete_pair_count = 300 paired observations under the shared_initial protocol. Host audit shows model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair invocation); the repair stage_count observed = 1. Missingness and contamination. No pairs were excluded; no provider/infrastructure dual‑call outages occurred; contamination checks and negative controls did not produce unexpected pass behavior. Primary outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667, guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The observed absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333; the paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI with seed = 1729 and B = 10000 is [0.00, 0.01]. Per‑stratum diagnostics. Per the stratification, low and medium strata each had baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; the single discordant episode was in the high stratum (high baseline = 99/100, guarded = 100/100). Repair diagnostic. The single guarded rescue invoked the permitted automated repair: the validator flagged a sequencing omission (missing required 'admin down' before VLAN/MTU change) and the constrained insertion edit corrected the sequence; the corrected candidate then passed deterministic validation. Cost footprint. The guarded pipeline incurred one additional repair stage call across 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating very low marginal model‑call cost for the observed deterministic rescue under the chosen repair budget and operator. Statistical interpretation. The inferential null (p = 1.0) reflects minimal discordance (m = 1) under the shared_initial estimand and the synthetic suite's near‑ceiling baseline; the bootstrap CI bounds the plausible absolute paired improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.
sections.discussion: Estimand and operational policy alignment. Conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent corresponds to operational policies that tightly constrain model calls for cost, latency, or governance reasons. Under such policies the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the same candidate; pipelines that permit resampling, verifier‑guided regeneration, or interactive steering address a different estimand and typically realize larger improvements by exploiting generator variance. Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration targeted detection of a 10 percentage‑point absolute improvement with planned power ≈0.8 based on a pilot to estimate discordance. The optional calibration pilot was not executed, and baseline single‑shot generation was near ceiling (299/300), producing few discordant pairs and limited power to detect small absolute improvements. This highlights the practical value of small calibration pilots when generator performance may be high on chosen suites. Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The solitary failure mode was a sequencing omission; other classes (reachability violations, ACL semantics) were not observed at scale in this synthetic suite. The guarded pipeline's marginal utility therefore depends on the deployment distribution of failure modes and on validator expressiveness: richer validators that check reachability or ACL semantics would likely increase observed rescues. Repair budget and operator design. We intentionally limited automated repair to a single constrained edit to measure bounded deterministic rescue; broader iterative repair or more expressive edit operators would increase rescue opportunities but change the estimand and operational cost. Practical implications for CI/CD and NetOps automation. Organizations must align evaluation estimands with operational choices: if pipelines permit multiple model calls or verifier‑guided regeneration, evaluations should allow resampling and interactive steering. If model calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate. The run's model_calls_used = 301 and repair_stage_count = 1 quantify the low marginal model cost observed for deterministic rescue here.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, archived paired comparison under the shared_initial estimand (300 paired intents stratified by difficulty) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator, baseline single‑shot generation passed deterministic validation in 299/300 cases and the guarded pipeline (validator + ≤1 repair) in 300/300 cases. The absolute paired improvement was 0.0033333 with exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0 and paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.00,0.01] (seed = 1729, B = 10000). Deterministic rescue occurred once via a single constrained insertion edit correcting a sequencing omission. Under the chosen synthetic suite and tight repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We release the preregistration, execution traces, validator logs, and analysis bundle to support reproducibility and to inform follow‑ups that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distributions, or repair budgets.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated deterministically; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase verifier marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing limited discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements relative to larger pre‑specified targets.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered pilot intended to estimate discordance and calibrate power was not run; no post‑preregistration sample‑size recalculation was performed.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions on a single LLM candidate and therefore does not measure verifier benefit that would arise from allowing independent alternative LLM candidates per condition (resampling or iterative generation).
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; larger or iterative repair strategies may yield different outcomes.
